kicker: BLACK FRIDAY HALF DAY · STOCKS CLOSED 1:00PM ET · CLOSE BRIEF
headline: Memory stocks lead a 1.6% half day rally; Nvidia lags.
lede: The S&P 500 closed at 7,298.34, +1.61%, and the Nasdaq rose 2.31% (Reuters), past the ±1.17% options had priced. Sandisk +16% and Micron +7.6% led while Nvidia added only 0.8%.
drivers: Cash closes: Sandisk +15.96%, Micron +7.60%, WDC +7.22%, SOXX +4.76%, SMH +4.17%. Reuters: investors flocked back to hard hit AI shares; one strategist called the market oversold.
Nvidia +0.80% to $150.49 after opening near +2% (Yahoo). FT reported Thursday that Nvidia told server makers to halt AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian countries.
Reuters: traders almost fully price a December hike after Q3 GDP was revised to 4.3%. The 10 year was near 4.93% in Reuters' late quote.
All 11 SPDR sector ETFs rose: tech XLK +2.80% led, utilities and health care +0.28% lagged. Reuters: volumes were thin after Thanksgiving.
picks: Close: S&P 7,298.34 (+1.61%), Nasdaq 24,129.50 (+2.31%), Dow 50,780.64 (+1.19%), per Reuters. All three posted weekly gains.
Memory led: Sandisk +15.96%, Micron +7.60%, WDC +7.22%, AMD +4.56%, SMH +4.17%. Nvidia +0.80% (Unusual Whales closes).
SPY made its session high, 729.15, in the final 5 minute bar.
Amazon up on strong Black Friday demand (Motley Fool); it closed +3.96%. Vertex fell about 5% after the FDA extended its kidney drug review (Reuters).
Session low: SPY 719.62 in the 10:05am bar; S&P day low 7,211.46 (Motley Fool data). Steady climb after.
Nvidia opened about 2% higher, then turned lower (Yahoo). FT reported Thursday it told Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia.
Reuters: traders almost fully price a Dec 9 hike. CME FedWatch was 98.9% Friday morning (Forbes). Already known.
Yields up: 10 year near 4.93%, 2 year near 4.70% in Reuters' late quotes. Bonds close 2:00pm.
Late quotes (Reuters): WTI $83.02 (−0.8%), Brent $90.31 (−1.5%), gold futures $3,650 (+3.2%).
TrendForce: limited demand visibility raises the risk of DRAM contract price declines in 2028. New.
October goods deficit $149.5B vs $133.1B expected (ActionForex). Known since the pre open brief.
Closes: Kospi +4.34%, Nikkei +2.11%, Shanghai +3.7% after China signaled market support (AP).
means: S&P closed at 7,298, just under the 7,304 OI gamma flip and the 7,310 flow call wall. Above them dealers lean long gamma.
Friday ran past the ±1.17% implied move. SPXW options price ±1.00% for Monday, about 73 points.
Leadership came from memory and chip equipment, not Nvidia. All 11 sector ETFs rose.
Back under 7,211, Friday's low, undoes the rebound; 7,183 is Wednesday's close.
calendar: ISM manufacturing (Nov) 55.2 consensus, prior 55.5. JOLTS 7.45M vs 7.523M prior. Fed's Bowman testifies
ADP (Nov) 80K consensus, prior 86K. Salesforce and Snowflake after close
Jobs (Nov): payrolls 90K consensus vs 165K prior, unemployment 4.1%

stories.why: Chips led November's drop; Reuters says investors flocked back to hard hit AI shares.
stories.read: An oversold bounce led by the hardest hit names, on thin volume.
stories.reacted: SPY rose from a 719.62 low at 10:05am to a 729.15 high in the last bar. The rebound began in overnight trading Thursday.
stories.confirm: Memory holds gains Monday and SMH stays above 435.

stories.h: Nvidia halts SE Asia server shipments
stories.what: FT: Nvidia told server makers including Dell and Supermicro to halt AI server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. A US rule on remote access to advanced chips took effect Nov 19.
stories.why: Nvidia's Singapore unit booked $104B of 2025 revenue (FT via TrendForce). It is unclear if the halt is temporary.
stories.read: Export rules now reach regional data center demand, not only China.
stories.reacted: First US session Friday: Nvidia opened near +2% and closed +0.80% at $150.49. No source ties the move to the report.
stories.changes: Adds export risk to Nvidia's demand outlook; watch license guidance and Huang's Dec 3 testimony.
stories.confirm: Nvidia or Commerce confirms licensing delays.
stories.invalid: Shipments resume or licenses are granted quickly.

stories.why: Memory pricing drives Micron, SK hynix and Samsung earnings.
stories.read: Long range caution, not a near term price cut.
stories.reacted: Memory stocks rallied anyway: Micron +7.60%, Sandisk +15.96%.
